newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger poll deadline passes, opposition hold back.
newsitem.headline: Niger poll deadline passes, opposition hold back.

text.p: The deadline for candidates to register in November's legislative election in Niger has passed with opposition parties still not signed up for the poll, interior ministry officials said.

Eight opposition parties, angry over the conduct of the July presidential election won by coup maker Ibrahim Bare Mainassara, let Wednesday's deadline pass without registering and without naming their representatives to a new electoral commission.

The November 23 election of the 83 members of the new national assembly is part of Mainassara's efforts to return the mainly Moslem West African state to multi-party politics following his coup in January.
It was not immediately clear whether further talks would be held to resolve the deadlock.
Mainassara, who toppled an elected president and government, scrapped the independent national electoral commission part way through the presidential election.

Eight opposition parties, grouped in the Front for the Restoration and Defence of Democracy, are demanding that the results of the July presidential election be annulled. They also want the scrapped electoral commission restored.
Further demands include reconstituted constitutional and supreme courts and U.N., Organisation of African Unity and European Union supervision of all Niger elections.
The ministry said that a total of 3.8 million voters were eligible to take part in the legislative election.
Candidates left in the race include independents and representatives of 12 minor parties.
